verdict.rationale: Self-hosting is a fair question for a SaaS platform like Glama's registry, gateway, and chat, so the axis applies. The evidence only describes Glama-managed hosting, where Glama builds and runs MCP servers on its own infrastructure and fronts them with its Gateway. Tunneling local MCP servers to the browser inspector via mcp-proxy is an adjacent feature and does not mean Glama itself can be self-hosted; no documentation shows a self-hostable distribution, deployment guide, or open-source release of the core product.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product
